key_insight: For clean, regenerable pages, decay can replace refresh: a per-row last-restore timestamp plus a trap on expiry gives zero refresh power with no cell change.
killer_doubt: Decode re-reads weights/KV every ~20-50 ms, past a 10 ms target, and refreshing a 10 ms die costs 64-128% of bandwidth at 32-64 Gb. The 3x Cs cut fails.
decisive_experiment: Trace row reuse intervals for 70B decode and training in Ramulator or an FPGA controller: what fraction of resident bytes is both regenerable and re-touched within 10/32/64 ms. ~$50k.
prior_art: Refrint and eDRAM-cache line decay (expired clean lines invalidated); Smart Refresh (2007); Flikker; our N-64 lease refresh and N-73 weight-streaming die.

key_insight: Retired fleet DRAM has no cell wear-out, so recovered bits use no wafer capacity and arrive within months during a ~4x price spike.
killer_doubt: Decapping and re-bumping molded FBGA dies damages pads and yield (est. 50-80% recovery), while whole retired DIMMs already plug into DDR4 CXL expanders with zero rework.
decisive_experiment: Chemically decap and re-bump 500 dies from retired RDIMMs. Compare BIST fallout, retention and VRT with the same lot reused as intact DIMMs behind a CXL controller. ~$100k.
prior_art: Marvell Structera X and Meta CXL reuse of whole retired DDR4 DIMMs; Microsoft GreenSKU; refurbished-DIMM resellers; failure-analysis decap labs.

key_insight: Strain-driven self-rolling turns a planar array into ~20 windings with one release etch, converting area into volume without deep etch or stack deposition.
killer_doubt: Rolling creates no bits: 20 turns need 20x the patterned flat area, so litho cost per bit is unchanged. A ~5 um radius bends a 100 nm stack ~1%.
decisive_experiment: Roll a 20-turn SiN/SiGe membrane carrying 1k IGZO gain cells at a university fab. Measure the Ioff tail, Vt shift and edge-contact yield before and after rolling. ~$200k.
prior_art: Schmidt group rolled-up nanomembrane electronics (IFW Dresden, from memory); our R08 I-00027 self-rolled array (DROP).

key_insight: Routing split lots across idle U.S. tools could cut a memory start-up's learning-cycle cost: renting hours instead of building a ~$50M pilot line.
killer_doubt: Cross-site lots break contamination rules (Cu, Au, alkali) and queue-time limits, since high-k and oxide-semiconductor interfaces drift in hours. NNCI sites already rent tools hourly.
decisive_experiment: Run one IGZO 2T0C short loop split across three NNCI sites and the same loop at a single site. Compare Vt spread, Ioff tail and cycle time. ~$150k.
prior_art: NSF NNCI (16 sites) hourly external access; Natcast/NSTC prototyping; MOSIS-style shuttles; Science Exchange-type service marketplaces.

key_insight: Matrix's ~4-mask-per-deck poly pillar stack is the right cost template, and swapping the antifuse for a capacitor removes the write-once failure.
killer_doubt: Hold bias ~V/2 sits across a poly-Si selector. Its own ms-scale refresh at ~50-100 fJ/bit per refresh is 70-140x DDR5's ~0.7 pW/bit refresh power.
decisive_experiment: Build 40 nm poly-Si n-p-n punch-through selectors with 1 fF MIM stubs on a 4-deck test chip. Map I(V/2) at 85 C to the 1e-6 tail and the write/hold current ratio. ~$300k.
prior_art: Matrix Semiconductor 3D poly-diode OTP (SanDisk); epitaxial-Si punch-through RRAM selector (IEEE EDL ~2012, from memory); our N-85 crested-barrier 1S1C.

key_insight: Thermophoresis is real and nearly size-independent: a 10 K/mm gradient gives ~0.03 cm/s outward drift, beating diffusion deposition for particles down to ~10-20 nm.
killer_doubt: FOUP/EFEM mini-environments already let ballrooms run ~ISO 5-6 (est.). Scanners hold wafers to ~mK, and a 10 K offset expands 300 mm Si ~8 um. AMC is untouched.
decisive_experiment: Count 20-100 nm particle adders on bare wafers held 0, 5, 10 and 20 K above ambient in an ISO-7 room and an ISO-4 room, using a surface scanner. ~$100k.
prior_art: Ye, Pui, Liu, Fissan et al. on thermophoretic wafer deposition (J. Aerosol Sci. ~1991, from memory); Sandia thermophoretic EUV-mask protection; SMIF/FOUP mini-environments.

key_insight: Decoding inside the stack makes contact count grow with log2(N), not N, so line-end area and staircase masks stop scaling with tier count.
killer_doubt: One etch through identical tiers cannot give each tier a unique code, and n-only IGZO decoders (~10-30 cm2/Vs) must swing VPP ~3 V onto long lines.
decisive_experiment: Build an 8-tier IGZO stack in which per-tier deposition (doping or thickness) sets a Vt code. Show 1-of-8 tier select with log2 lines and measure margin at 85 C. ~$400k.
prior_art: Our N-47 Vt-coded in-stack tier decoder (ALIVE) supplies the missing per-tier code; 3D NAND in-channel string/ground select transistors.

key_insight: Stamps place thousands of thin tiles per cycle with no hybrid-bond aligner. Lithographic vias at ~10 um pitch still give ~1e4 links/mm2 at ~0.1-0.3 pJ/bit.
killer_doubt: DRAM over hot logic: retention halves per ~10 C, so 105 C junctions mean ~4x the refresh of 85 C. DRAM wafers lack a release layer and need carrier laser-debond.
decisive_experiment: Thin a commercial DRAM wafer to ~10 um on a laser-release carrier and transfer-print 1 mm2 tiles onto a dummy logic wafer. Planarize, add vias, then measure print yield, placement and retention-tail shift. ~$600k.
prior_art: X-Celeprint/X-FAB uTP foundry for III-V, GaN and photonics, <1 um misalignment and up to 99% yield (via search snippet); no DRAM-on-logic uTP found.

key_insight: Same physics win as I-04377: charge shifts through an IGZO channel, so wear is gate stress only, and IGZO's low generation holds packets for >200 s.
killer_doubt: 2-bit packets over ~300-600 transfers need CTE >=0.9999, but imec's IGZO CCD shows >98% (0.98^300 ~0.2%). 2-phase operation needs built-in barriers that a hole liner cannot implant.
decisive_experiment: Measure 2-bit packet error after 50, 100 and 300 transfers on imec-style vertical IGZO CCD strings at 25-85 C with 1-50 MHz clocks. ~$400k.
prior_art: imec IGZO 3D CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024; 3D demo 2026; CTE >98%, >4 MHz); our N-08; Intel 2416 and Fairchild CCD memories.

key_insight: Channel shifting dodges the write-endurance wall. Ganging every fourth tier onto four phase rails removes the staircase: one critical hole mask, ~50 bits/hole, ~2-3x 1b density.
killer_doubt: 2 GHz fails: 50 ganged planes per phase are ~0.35-3.5 nF (6-60 W at 2 GHz). At imec's >4 MHz, a 100-transfer access is ~25 us. CTE needs >=0.9995.
decisive_experiment: On a 16-tier stack of selectively etchable gate materials, prove selective-recess phase contacts with no staircase. Then measure vertical IGZO-liner CTE against clock (1-50 MHz) and temperature (25-85 C). ~$700k.
prior_art: imec IGZO 3D CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024; 3-word-line 3D demo 2026); our N-08; Fairchild F464 and Intel 2416 CCD memories.

key_insight: A closed-flux circumferential NiFe bit around a vertical conductor is stray-field-free and non-destructively readable. One hole mask with aqueous MACE and plating avoids rare gases.
killer_doubt: Inductive read collapses: a 10x50 nm NiFe ring links ~5e-16 Wb, so a 1 ns tilt gives ~0.1-0.25 uV against >=2 uV core-line thermal noise. TMR read makes it N-82.
decisive_experiment: Plate 10 nm NiFe in 100 nm holes through 8 doped-Si planes. Pulse one plane and measure the core-line EMF with a low-noise amplifier against 4kTR noise. ~$150k; expect sub-uV.
prior_art: 1960s-70s plated-wire memory (Univac; Apollo/Skylab-era systems); our R09 I-04150 and R21 I-08865 vertical magnetic tubes (both DROP).

key_insight: Frozen weights need no writes or refresh, so a generic base wafer personalized only in its via layers puts model weights in read-only bits beside compute.
killer_doubt: Diode-less via crosspoints short rows to columns, and sneak paths through ~50 ohm vias defeat reading. Multibeam writing ~2e13 vias per wafer per level takes tens to hundreds of hours.
decisive_experiment: Tape out a 28-40 nm 2-deck via-ROM crossbar with and without per-via oxide diodes. Measure read margin against array size (64-1,024 lines). ~$300k MPW.
prior_art: Logic mask/via ROM; Matrix poly-diode 3D OTP; our R16 I-03028 (ADVANCE, ArF via mask) and R18 I-02068 (DROP, sneak paths).
